newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia Nusamba offers to buy stake in Freeport.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia Nusamba offers to buy stake in Freeport.

text.p: Indonesia's PT Nusamba Mineral Industri announced on Wednesday a tender offer to buy a 50.479-percent stake in PT Indocopper Investama Corporation for $311.8 million.
"The company intends to own 10,814,900 shares or 50.479 percent of the total paid-up capital of the targetted company," Nusamba said in an advertisement in the Harian Neraca daily.

The Nusamba Group is 80 percent owned by three foundations headed by President Suharto. Timber baron Muhammad "Bob" Hasan, who heads Nusamba, and Suharto's eldest son Sigit Harjojudanto each have a 10-percent stake.
Nusamba said it was offering $28.829 per share in PT Indocopper. In the advertisement Bank Umum Nasional said Nusamba had sufficient funds for the tender offer.
PT Indocopper has a 9.36-percent stake in PT Freeport Indonesia, which operates one of the world's largest copper and gold mines in eastern Irian Jaya province.
Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc of the United States owns 81.28 percent of Freeport Indonesia, with the remaining 9.36 percent held by the Indonesian government.
Well-diversified Bakrie & Brothers has a 49-percent stake in PT Indocopper. Bakrie had said it had not decided yet on selling its stake in PT Indocopper.
Bakrie Investindo, which is part of the Bakrie group, has a 1.5-percent stake in PT Indocopper, Freeport McMoRan 49 percent and the remaining 0.5 percent is held by the public.
A Bakrie spokesman said Bakrie & Brothers would hold a meeting of its board of directors on Wednesday to decide on a response to the tender offer.
